findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the CI-step deletion with _build-and-test.yml:847-850: the 'MCP model schema drift gate' step has no if-present guard, so confirm how main's workflow tolerates the deleted check_mcp_models.py (add a guard, delete the step in the same change, or correct the ee2a-guard premise).
evidence: _build-and-test.yml:847-850 — the drift-gate step is `run: python -m rebar.schemas.check_mcp_models --check` with no if-present guard
_build-and-test.yml:820-824 — check_server_manifest step HAS an `if [ ! -f ... ] exit 0` guard, showing the guard is per-step and not present on the drift gate

_build-and-test.yml:852-857 — comment states the 'old if-present guard' was removed and tree-skew is now handled by `make lint` running the patchset's own Makefile, contradicting the plan's premise that the drift gate carries such a guard
findings.finding: The plan's justification for deleting the 'MCP model schema drift gate' CI step rests on an if-present guard that step does not have. The step at _build-and-test.yml:847-850 unconditionally runs `python -m rebar.schemas.check_mcp_models --check` with no `if [ ! -f ... ]` guard (unlike check_server_manifest.py:820-824 which does), and the comment at 852-857 says that guard pattern was intentionally dropped. If, as the plan itself asserts, Gerrit runs main's workflow on the change's tree, deleting check_mcp_models.py makes that step fail with module-not-found until main also drops the step.
findings.location: Scope section: 'the CI step (after main carries its ee2a if-present guard: Gerrit runs main's workflow on the change's tree)'
scenarios: CI runs main's unchanged workflow against a change tree that has already deleted check_mcp_models.py; the drift-gate step aborts with ModuleNotFoundError
findings.suggested_fix: Either (a) land the step deletion together with an if-present guard mirroring check_server_manifest.py:820-824 before removing the module, or (b) drop the inaccurate 'carries its ee2a if-present guard' claim and state the real tree-skew handling the workflow actually uses.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the `gate_run.status` enum vocabulary (`running`, `passed`, `failed`, `attaching`, `unknown`) in the new schema so the advertised contract is as tight as the library emitter.
evidence: Plan lists `status` with no enum members.

`rebar.llm.gate_run_status` emits a bounded vocabulary: gate_runs.py:324-326 docstring 'status is running / passed / failed / attaching / unknown', with literals at gate_runs.py:342-343 ('attaching','unknown') and gate_runs.py:310 ('failed').

Because the plan's whole thesis is that the advertised outputSchema is the sole validated contract (mcp lowlevel server validate), an under-constrained `status: string` lets any value through — the second-contract drift the plan is deleting.
findings.finding: The new `gate_run` schema declares a required `status` field but the plan never specifies its enum vocabulary, so an executor could author it as a bare string and re-open the drift the plan exists to eliminate.
scenarios: Author writes `gate_run.schema.json` with `status: {type: string}`; a typo'd library status would validate and the canonical-contract guarantee is lost.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define the `verify_completion_status.verdict` vocabulary against the actual `compute_validity` verdict set (certified, unsigned, stale-reopened, stale-material, not-closed, …) — or declare it a free `string` with a comment — rather than the narrower tool-docstring pair, and reconcile the docstring.
evidence: Plan lists `verdict` with no vocabulary.

`rebar.llm.verify_completion_status` sets verdict from `validity.get('verdict')` (gate_runs.py:417) whose docstring enumerates 'certified only when valid RIGHT NOW, else the classifier reason (stale-reopened / stale-material / not-closed / unsigned / …)' (gate_runs.py:377-379).

The MCP tool docstring at _mcp_reads.py:189-191 says only 'verdict is certified or unsigned', which is narrower than the library — pinning the enum to that pair would reject stale verdicts at startup/validation.
findings.finding: The new `verify_completion_status` schema declares a required `verdict` field with no vocabulary, and the one hint in-tree (the tool docstring 'verdict is certified or unsigned') understates what the library emits — the real emitter also returns compute_validity classifier reasons (stale-reopened/stale-material/not-closed/…), so a two-value enum would make the SDK validator reject legitimate results.
scenarios: A stale-reopened completion attestation makes the tool return verdict='stale-reopened'; a {certified,unsigned} enum raises a validation error and the tool call fails.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the `gate_run.findings` sub-object shape (`sidecar_type`, `readable`, `reason`, `reviewed_at`, `latest_reviewed_at`, optional `job_started_at`) and its `reason` string vocabulary in the new schema.
evidence: Plan names `findings` but gives no shape.

`_review_result_status` returns a fixed object `{sidecar_type, readable, reason, reviewed_at, latest_reviewed_at}` plus optional `job_started_at` (gate_runs.py:250-256,279), with a bounded `reason` vocabulary (run-<status>, current-review-result-sidecar, review-result-sidecar-missing, run-failed, sidecar-not-emitted, review-result-generation-unknown).
The gate_status tool docstring instructs callers to branch on `findings.readable` (_mcp_reads.py:208), so this is an agent-consumed decision rule whose schema must co-locate the field it keys on.
findings.finding: The new `gate_run` schema lists an optional `findings` field but the plan never specifies its sub-object shape or the reason-string vocabulary that an LLM poller reads to decide readiness, leaving a structured sub-contract undefined.
findings.location: Approach — `gate_run` 'optional … `findings`'; AC references 'Read plan findings only after findings.readable is true'
scenarios: Poller validates a gate_status result; `findings` is `{}`-shaped or omits `readable`, and the advertised schema cannot catch it.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Verify (and specify) that `install_canonical_output_schemas` updates the schema surfaced by `list_tools()` (the FastMCP Tool.output_schema / wire types.Tool.outputSchema), not only `fn_metadata.output_schema`, since _mcp_health.py:170 and the coverage test both read the registration-time Tool surface.
evidence: _mcp_health.py:170-172: 'the SDK already built this tool's fn_metadata (and therefore its argument model and output schema) from the original callable at registration time'
test_mcp_output_schema_coverage.py:170 reads `t.outputSchema` on list_tools() results (the wire types.Tool), not fn_metadata

AC: 'Every tool that advertises an outputSchema advertises the canonical file content (the diff test)' and 'list_tools() count is 64 and exactly 11 tools lack an outputSchema' both read the advertised wire schema
FastMCP Tool exists (mcp.server.fastmcp.tools.base.Tool) and typically stores a registration-time output_schema distinct from fn_metadata
findings.finding: The plan sets only `get_tool(name).fn_metadata.output_schema`, but the advertised schema consumers (list_tools()->types.Tool.outputSchema, read by the diff test and the coverage-count AC) are populated from the FastMCP Tool object's own output_schema field, computed at registration time; mutating fn_metadata alone may not update the advertised schema.
scenarios: After install_canonical_output_schemas runs, list_tools() still returns the auto-derived (or empty) outputSchema because Tool.output_schema was snapshotted at registration and never re-read from fn_metadata
The diff test passes against fn_metadata but the wire payload advertises a stale/absent schema
findings.suggested_fix: Set the inlined schema on the Tool object's own output_schema field (and any cached wire schema) in addition to fn_metadata.output_schema, or construct it on fn_metadata BEFORE the Tool snapshots it; add an assertion in the install step that `get_tool(name).output_schema == inline_schema(...)` so a non-propagating mutation fails at startup.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Record the back-out posture for the advertised-outputSchema change (e.g. the change is a single git-revertible cutover; note any client that was validating the old mirror schema) in Context or Scope.
evidence: Approach: 'add `common.$defs.push_status` ... `$ref`'d from claim/create/sign/transition results'; 'Null-vs-absent: a key the library omits is absent, never null.'
AC: 'Non-codebase: `docs/release-notes.md` lists every field that was null and is now absent, per tool family.' — documents the field change but not a reversibility/back-out mechanism.
T4 remedy requires an explicit rollback/expand-contract, not acknowledgement alone.
findings.finding: The advertised MCP `outputSchema` is changing shape for existing MCP clients (e.g. results gain a required/`$ref`'d `push_status`, and null-valued keys become absent), yet the plan states no back-out/rollback posture for this consumer-facing wire-contract change — only a release-note of null->absent fields.
scenarios: A downstream MCP client validating structured results against the previously-advertised schema breaks when a newly-required/added field appears or a previously-null field is now absent.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sentence stating the cutover is atomic and git-revertible, and that the advertised schema change is intentional/documented in release-notes, satisfying the expand-contract/rollback expectation.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Pin/raise the mcp lower bound to the exact version where `FuncMetadata.{output_schema,output_model,wrap_output}` and the lowlevel `jsonschema.validate(tool.outputSchema)` path exist, cite that version's SDK file:line, reconcile the `mcp==1.16.0` scanner pins, and route verification of these private attributes through a short SPIKE before deleting the mirror.
evidence: Plan cites 'jsonschema.validate against tool.outputSchema, mcp/server/lowlevel/server.py:566-575, mcp 1.29.0'
pyproject.toml:84 `mcp = ["mcp>=1.28.1,<2", ...]`; pyproject.toml:241 `"mcp>=1.28.1,<2"` — floating range, not 1.29.0

infra/compose/review-scanners.linux-{arm64,amd64}.requirements.txt:287 `mcp==1.16.0` — structured-output/outputSchema validation and the fn_metadata.output_schema/output_model/wrap_output attributes may not exist at this version

Repo precedent (_mcp_health.py:159,201-211) touches `_tool_manager`/`fn_metadata` only for offload (`tool.fn`, `is_async`); it never reads/writes `output_schema`, `output_model`, or `wrap_output` — a NEW SDK surface

Prior plan-review cache entries explicitly flagged: 'Pin the exact mcp version the fn_metadata.output_schema / output_model / wrap_output override ... were [introduced]' and 'cite the mcp 1.29.0 SDK file:line that defines fn_metadata.output_schema / output_model / wrap_output'

EVIDENCE CLASS: Partially-verified (mcp + jsonschema EXISTS; the specific private-attribute surface and its presence across the pinned version range is Unverified and internally Contradicted on version)
findings.finding: The plan's core mechanism depends on three private MCP SDK FuncMetadata attributes (`fn_metadata.output_schema`, `output_model`, `wrap_output`) and a specific lowlevel validation path (`server.py:566-575`) cited as mcp 1.29.0, but the dependency is pinned as a floating range `mcp>=1.28.1,<2` (pyproject.toml:84,241) and the infra scanners pin `mcp==1.16.0` — so the asserted SDK surface is unverified across the actually-installable version range and may not exist on the lower bound.
findings.location: Approach — `install_canonical_output_schemas(mcp)` ... sets `mcp._tool_manager.get_tool(name).fn_metadata.output_schema`, asserting `output_model is not None` and `wrap_output == (kind != 'object')`
scenarios: Prod/CI installs mcp 1.28.1 or a 1.3x where `FuncMetadata` lacks `output_schema`/`output_model`/`wrap_output` or spells them differently → `install_canonical_output_schemas` raises AttributeError at startup, or the assertion fails
Scanner images on mcp 1.16.0 run the new code path and crash on an SDK that predates structured outputSchema validation entirely
findings.suggested_fix: Add a startup-probe/SPIKE that imports `FuncMetadata` and asserts the three attributes plus the lowlevel validation branch on the pinned mcp, bump `pyproject.toml` to `mcp>=<verified-version>,<2`, and update the scanner requirements off 1.16.0; cite the observed SDK source lines (not the 1.29.0 claim alone) in the Approach.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State, per kind, exactly what the array/list_of tool body returns (a bare list that the SDK wraps under `result`, vs. a pre-wrapped `{"result": …}` dict) and confirm it is wrapped exactly once against the inlined `{"result": [S]}` schema.
evidence: Plan: array = canonical array schema under `{"result": …}`; list_of = `{"result": [S]}`
Plan: bodies 'return the library dict or list unchanged' annotated `-> list[dict[str, Any]]`
The MCP SDK wraps non-object structured results under `{"result": …}` when wrap_output is true; a list return annotation sets wrap_output true, so the SDK adds the wrapper itself
If the inlined schema is `{"result":[S]}` AND the body already returns `{"result":[...]}`, the SDK wrapper would nest it to `{"result":{"result":[...]}}`
findings.finding: The plan does not reconcile FastMCP's own `{"result": …}` wrapping (driven by wrap_output / a list return annotation) with the inlined canonical schema shape `{"result": [S]}` for the array/list_of kinds, risking a double-wrap that fails validation.
findings.location: Approach — `array`/`list_of` kinds, `wrap_output == (kind != "object")`, 'Tool bodies return the library dict or list unchanged, annotated … -> list[dict[str, Any]]'
scenarios: list_tickets returns `{"result":[...]}` and wrap_output=True wraps again, failing validation against `{"result":[S]}`
Or the body returns a bare list but the schema expects a top-level `{"result":...}` object the SDK did not add because wrap_output was false
findings.suggested_fix: Make array/list_of bodies return the bare list and let wrap_output=True add the single `{"result": …}` layer (so the SDK-produced structured content matches `{"result":[S]}`), and assert in a test that the structured content is not double-nested.
